findings.claim: The ledger answer (L6) says to add an opt-out setting, but the change emits ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally on supported targets. There is no opt-out option, so existing users who do not want the attribute (or who rely on coverage of generated code) cannot disable it.

receipt_plan.detail: Cite L6 ('Add an opt-out setting') and show that no new generator option or MSBuild property is read by any template or by the generator options class.

findings.claim: The TransformUtilities change alters whitespace emitted after a nesting type's constraints (`{` becomes `{\r\n`). This changes generated output for every nested or generic-nested type, which affects users who check in or snapshot generated output. It is not part of the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests for nested generic types with constraints and diff the output against base. Confirm the only differences are the attribute lines and the extra newline.

findings.claim: The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard assumes ExcludeFromCodeCoverage exists on every other target. A consumer targeting netstandard2.1 or an old netcoreapp, or an assembly built with a custom TFM, may lack the type (it was added in netcoreapp2.0 and netstandard2.1), and the guard would not exclude it. Generated code would then fail to compile, which is a breaking build error. The preprocessor symbols (NETCOREAPP2_0_OR_GREATER or NETSTANDARD2_1_OR_GREATER) are not consulted.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile generated output in a project targeting netcoreapp1.x (or a TFM without System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) and check for CS0234 or CS0246. At minimum, compile for netstandard2.1 and net6.0.
